chunks: Yūnus, from Ibn Miskān, from Abī Baṣīr, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who was killed while he owed a debt and had no property: do his heirs have the right to forgo his blood in favor of his killer while he still has a debt?

He عليه السلام said: “Indeed, the holders of the debt are the claimants against the killer. So if his heirs forgo his blood in favor of the killer, they become liable for the blood money to the creditors; otherwise, no.”

key_terms.أَوْلِيَائِهِ: The legal heirs or blood-relatives entitled to act regarding the victim’s blood claim.
key_terms.دَمَهُ: His blood, meaning the legal claim arising from his killing.
key_terms.دَيْنٌ: A financial debt owed by the deceased.
key_terms.لِلْقَاتِلِ: In favor of the killer, by waiving the blood claim against him.
key_terms.ٱلدِّيَةَ: The blood money due in compensation for killing.
key_terms.ٱلْغُرَمَاءُ: The creditors to whom the deceased owed money.

ai.seo_question: If a murdered person had unpaid debts and no wealth, can his heirs pardon the killer without compensating the creditors?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a murdered person who died indebted and left no property. It states that the creditors have a claim connected to the killer through the diyah, and if the heirs pardon the killer, they must guarantee the diyah for the creditors.
